name: Epoprostenol
route_note: Continuous intravenous infusion via a central venous catheter and portable pump

discovery.by: Salvador Moncada, John Vane and colleagues at the Wellcome Research Laboratories
discovery.note: Identified as an unstable arachidonic-acid metabolite produced by blood-vessel walls that inhibits platelet aggregation and dilates vessels.

tagline: Continuously infused prostacyclin, the first drug shown to prolong survival in PAH
summary: Epoprostenol is synthetic prostacyclin, a natural vasodilator and inhibitor of platelet aggregation. Given by continuous intravenous infusion, it was the first therapy approved for pulmonary arterial hypertension and the first shown in a randomised trial to improve survival.
mechanism: Epoprostenol activates the prostacyclin (IP) receptor on vascular smooth muscle and platelets. The Gs-coupled receptor raises cAMP, causing vasodilation of pulmonary and systemic arteries and inhibiting platelet aggregation.

It may also have antiproliferative effects on vascular smooth muscle. Its half-life is only a few minutes, so it must be given continuously; interruption can cause dangerous rebound pulmonary hypertension.
uses: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO group I, NYHA class III–IV)

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Moncada, Vane and co-workers describe prostacyclin in Nature.

history.title: Nobel Prize
history.detail: John Vane shares the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for prostaglandin research.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: FDA approves Flolan for primary pulmonary hypertension.

history.title: Survival benefit
history.detail: A randomised trial (Barst et al., NEJM) shows improved exercise capacity and survival in primary pulmonary hypertension.

history.title: Room-temperature formulation
history.detail: FDA approves Veletri, a more stable formulation, and the first generic epoprostenol.

pk.metabolism: Rapid hydrolysis at neutral pH and enzymatic degradation to 6-keto-PGF1α and other metabolites

serious: Rebound pulmonary hypertension on abrupt interruption

facts: Epoprostenol is chemically identical to prostacyclin made by vascular endothelium.
Patients typically carry a battery-powered infusion pump around the clock.
